subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
skillName: Drawing Geometric Shapes with Given Conditions
intro: Each problem asks you to test a single rule. For three side lengths, a triangle exists only when the two shorter sides add up to more than the longest side (the triangle inequality). For three angle measures, a triangle exists only when the three angles add up to exactly $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: Can a triangle be drawn with side lengths $3\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$, and $5\text{ cm}$? Answer yes or no and explain.

steps: Identify the two shorter sides ($3$ and $4$) and the longest side ($5$).
Add the two shorter sides: $3 + 4 = 7$.
Compare to the longest side: $7 > 5$, so the triangle inequality holds.
Yes, a triangle can be drawn.

items.prompt: Can a triangle be drawn with side lengths $2\text{ cm}$, $3\text{ cm}$, and $9\text{ cm}$? Answer yes or no and explain.

steps: The two shorter sides are $2$ and $3$; the longest side is $9$.
Add the two shorter sides: $2 + 3 = 5$.
Compare to the longest side: $5 < 9$, so the triangle inequality fails.
No, a triangle cannot be drawn because the two short sides are too short to meet.

items.prompt: Can a triangle have interior angles measuring $60^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $60^\circ$? Answer yes or no and explain.

steps: The three interior angles of a triangle must total $180^\circ$.
Add the angles: $60 + 60 + 60 = 180$.
The sum is exactly $180^\circ$, so the angles are valid.
Yes, this is a triangle (an equilateral triangle).

items.prompt: Can a triangle have interior angles measuring $40^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $90^\circ$? Answer yes or no and explain.

steps: The three interior angles of a triangle must total $180^\circ$.
Add the angles: $40 + 60 + 90 = 190$.
The sum is $190^\circ$, which is not $180^\circ$.
No, these angles cannot form a triangle.
